SUBJECT / SUJET CATHOLIC LEADER ENDORSES YMCA 


WORD COUNT/ NOMBRE DE MOTS 240 


YMCA OF MONTREAL 
FOR/COMMUNIQUE AU NOM D 


AT WILL 
FOR PUBLICATION/PUBLIABLE 


POUR aOnEEnE Aven 
COMMUNIQU 
/CONTACT W. SHER 


Father Irénée Beaubien has joined the growing number 
of Roman Catholics who recognize that the YMCA can contribute 
increasingly to the elimination of prejudices of various kinds. 

Father Beaubien is Director of the Montreal Ecumenical 
Centre and a member of the board of the National Secretariat 
on Ecumenism. 

He considers the YMCA as one of the leading world 
associations dedicated to serving the spiritual, intellectual 
and physical needs of people, especially youth. 

"The time has come for the Y and similarly-motivated 
Roman Catholic associations to enter into dialogue, and see 
what can be done, cooperatively, to better serve the needs of 
the community", says Father Beaubien. 


Continued 


a 


"The attitude of the Vatican Council makes it evident 
that Catholics should try to cooperate, as much as possible, 
with due regard to local circumstances, with any association 
that tries to foster mutual understanding so that the common 
needs of human beings will be better served", he emphasizes. 

"In Canada, understanding should be developed not only 
between people of various beliefs but also between citizens of 
French, English and other cultures. Here the YMCA has a 
definite role to play. 

"We know that at the present time the Montreal YMCA has 
undertaken a study to assess its policy in the light of the 
changing needs of our time. This effort deserves our sympathy 
and our cooperation" concludes Father Beaubien. 


- 30 4 
November 21, 1966
